description: A four-panel composite illustrative figure (no axes, no scale bars, no printed numeric values) built from two grey-scale micrographs and their colour-coded ground-truth annotations, arranged to contrast two classes of material micrograph. (b) centre-left, labelled "Polycrytalline" with "Pure iron" below, is a grey-scale micrograph showing a dense network of dark grain boundaries enclosing light grains; a blue square box in it is linked by blue dashed lines to (a) top-left, labelled "Ground truth", the same field with every grain filled in a different pastel colour and carrying a red dot marker. (c) centre-right, labelled "Multiphase" with "Supperalloy" below, is a grey-scale micrograph of a light cellular/dendritic network separating darker cell interiors; its orange square box is linked by orange dashed lines to (d) top-right, "Ground truth", a colour-coded phase map also dotted with red markers. Two banner strips close the figure: left, "No voids between grains and boundaries" with "No voids" in red; right, "Gaps between different phase regions" with "Gaps" in red. The argument: polycrystalline fields are grains plus boundaries with no background, multiphase fields are phase regions separated by gaps plus background, and the red dots are prompt points.

subfigures.description: Colour-coded 'Ground truth' annotation of a polycrystalline microstructure: irregular grains each filled with a distinct pastel colour (green, pink, blue, tan, red) and each marked with a red dot; blue dashed lines connect it to the blue box in panel (b), identifying it as the magnified annotation of that field.

Grey-scale micrograph labelled 'Polycrytalline' (banner) and 'Pure iron' (label below), showing a dense network of dark grain-boundary lines enclosing light grains with no dark background regions; a blue square box outlines the region enlarged in (a).

Grey-scale micrograph labelled 'Multiphase' (banner) and 'Supperalloy' (label below), showing a light cellular/dendritic network of ridges separating darker cell interiors; an orange square box outlines the region enlarged in (d).

Colour-coded 'Ground truth' annotation of the multiphase field: each phase region filled with a different colour (grey-blue, green, red-brown, purple) and marked with red dots; orange dashed lines connect it to the orange box in (c).

observations.observation: Panel (b) is a grey-scale micrograph labelled 'Polycrytalline' with 'Pure iron' printed beneath it, showing dark grain boundaries enclosing light grains.
Panel (a), labelled 'Ground truth', shows the same polycrystalline field as (b) with each grain filled in a different pastel colour and marked by a red dot.
A blue square box in (b) is connected by blue dashed lines to (a), indicating (a) is a magnified ground-truth annotation of that boxed sub-region.
Panel (c) is a grey-scale micrograph labelled 'Multiphase' with 'Supperalloy' printed beneath it, showing a light cellular network separating darker regions.
Panel (d), labelled 'Ground truth', colour-codes the phase regions of (c) and carries red dot markers; orange dashed lines connect it to an orange box drawn inside (c).
The bottom-left banner reads 'No voids between grains and boundaries', with the words 'No voids' printed in red.
The bottom-right banner reads 'Gaps between different phase regions', with the word 'Gaps' printed in red.
No scale bar, magnification value, axis label or numeric value is printed in any of the four panels.
The red dots are distributed inside individual grains in (a) and inside individual phase regions in (d), consistent with them being prompt points rather than measurements.
The caption states that for a polycrystalline image boundaries separate grains that adhere closely without voids, containing two classes — grain and its boundary, with no background.
The caption states that for a multiphase image gaps usually remain between phase regions dispersing across the whole image, giving multiple classes — different phase types plus background.
The citing text states that the conspicuous difference between the two micrograph kinds stems from whether there are voids or gaps between multiple target objects.

The citing text states that regions of interest can be effectively segmented as long as the prompt points abide by their features and distribution, which the proposed structure-aware prompt point generation of MatSAM can universally provide.
